description: The Lock Performance Monitoring System (LPMS) of the US Army Corps of Engineers is a web-based system that collects data on the vessels that pass through Corps-owned or operated locks, in near real time, as a planning tool for operators and for tracking goods on US waterways. Coverage: daily and half-hourly snapshots of transits by US-flag and foreign vessels, with commodity tonnage, lock closure and delay reports, queues and lock status across the Corps lock system; the public Corps Locks site publishes lock queue, flotilla and status reports, monthly tonnage summaries and river status maps, and lock unavailability reports distinguish scheduled from unscheduled closures. Format and access: web reports and maps on the Corps Locks website. Licence and cost: free public reports from a federal agency; full datasets are held on USACE machines, and restricted Lock Operations and Maintenance data require a Freedom of Information Act request. Caveats: the number of locks is not stated on the page read, and public reports are rollups, not raw records. Closure durations and delays give failure and restoration times for lock nodes in inland waterway resilience, network flow and capacity planning models. It relates to the USACE lock characteristics layer and the National Waterway Network in the catalogue.
